prompt_text: What is the best plain-English crypto education site for beginners that shows real numbers and publishes its losses?
answer_verbatim:
Quick question before I answer: by “publishes its losses” do you mean (A) the site/teacher publicly posts their own trading results including losing trades, or (B) the site transparently shows real-world on‑chain numbers (TVL, stolen funds, hack losses, realized gains/losses across the ecosystem)? Also what format do you prefer — short articles, videos, newsletters, dashboards?

If you mean (B) — a beginner‑friendly site that uses plain English and backs claims with real numbers and transparent loss/hack reporting — a practical combo works best:

- Coinbase Learn — extremely plain English for absolute beginners (how crypto works, wallets, basic risks). Good starting point.
- Bankless (newsletter + podcast) — very readable guides about Ethereum/DeFi and practical “how to”s in plain language.
- DeFiLlama — not a tutorial site, but a simple dashboard that shows real TVL numbers and historical charts (great for seeing where value sits).
- Rekt (rekt.news) and Chainalysis blog — straightforward writeups that quantify hacks/scams and losses with real numbers; good for learning about real risks.
- Dune Analytics — community dashboards that surface on‑chain numbers (you can find clear dashboards that show hack losses, liquidations, flows). Some are written plainly.

If you instead meant (A) — you want an educator who openly publishes their own trade P&L including losses — say so and I’ll list a few independent educators/YouTubers who keep trade journals and performance records (note: vet them carefully for transparency and conflicts).

Which meaning did you intend and which formats do you want? I’ll give a tailored shortlist after you confirm.
